 MSU students broadly unaware of Board of Trustees candidates on Election Day
 Belle Potter 
  and  Julia Roeder 
 November 4, 2026
 Michigan State students vote in person during the 2026 Midterm election at the Kellogg Hotel & Conference Center in East Lansing, Mich., on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.
 — Photo by
 Sebastien Desiderio 
 | The State News
 A summer of headlines detailing discord within the Michigan State University Board of Trustees came to a head on Election Day with two incumbents vying to reclaim their seats. 
 Outside of each on-campus precinct, The State News surveyed student voters on how they voted in the election, including the MSU Board of Trustees race. Over 30 students said they were not educated enough to know which candidate they voted for, or didn’t feel confident enough to vote in that race at all.  
 With 93% of the vote tallied, Board Chair Brianna Scott and Trustee Kelly Tebay Zemke will retain their seats on the board, the Associated Press called early Wednesday. Scott earned 26.7% of the statewide vote with 2.3 million votes, and Tebay Zemke obtained 25.6% of the vote with 2.2 million votes. 
 Trailing behind them were former Novi City Council member Julie Maday and former state Sen. Roger Victory, R-Hudsonville, each with 22% of the vote and a difference of 4,004. 
 Physics freshman Alfina Krider, who lives in East Neighborhood and voted at the IM East precinct, chose not to cast a vote for the trustees' race due to a lack of awareness of their policies. Though she researched prior to voting, she found the information to be “vague” and “contradictory.” 
 “It’s better to not take a stand than to take one and be incorrect because at that point you're just guessing,” Krider said. 
 Animal science sophomore Ella Hebbes, who lives in River Trail Neighborhood and voted at the IM East location, said she did not vote in the MSU Board of Trustees race. 
 "I just didn't know enough about it to feel confident to make a choice," Hebbes said.  
 Some students said they tried their best to become educated on the race in order to cast their vote.  
 Psychology and criminal justice freshman Moe VandenHeuvel and music performance freshman Ezra Marsh, who both live in East Neighborhood and voted at the IM East location, did their own individual “digging” before casting their ballots. 
 Both VandenHeuvel and Marsh voted for the candidates who stand for making “housing less expensive” and the board’s priorities more “visible.” However, neither could remember the names of the candidates they voted for.  
 “I mainly voted for the Board of Trustees because of all of the crazy drama that’s been going on,” VandenHeuvel said. “It’s weird, and there’s something going on there.”

 After watching President Kevin Guskiewicz blame the MSU Board for his now-reversed departure to Clemson University, horticulture sophomore Tabby Bartrum said she knew she wanted to do research on the election candidates. 
 “Buzzwords” stood out to Bartrum on Tebay Zemke and Scott’s campaign websites.

 Social studies and secondary education senior Vincent Delgado, who lives off campus and voted at the Union precinct, submitted his ballot for Tebay Zemke and Scott.  
 Although Delgado has concerns about the two current board members' handling of university leadership, President Guskiewicz’s salary increase and budget cuts have affected student workers.  
 With his vote for Scott and Tebay Zemke, Delgado stressed that “does not mean I will not criticize and try to push them to make better changes than what they’re doing right now.”
